fixes.explanation: That's the very first thing out of the LORD's mouth: "Woe to the shepherds who destroy and scatter the sheep of My pasture!" A shepherd's whole job is keeping the flock together and safe. These shepherds did the exact opposite.
Selling them at a market isn't what the LORD says, friend. He says the shepherds "…destroy and scatter…" the sheep. The text doesn't mention a market at all.

That's right, baker. The LORD says "…the sheep of My pasture!" in verse 1, and in verse 2 He calls them "My flock" and "My people." The sheep are His. The shepherds were only tending what belonged to Him.

Those are the shepherds who just heard "Woe" in verse 1, so they're not the ones getting the rescue job. The LORD says, "…I Myself will gather the remnant of My flock…" The text gives that job to Him, not to them.
Soldiers sound strong, but they're not in this verse. The LORD says He'll raise up "…shepherds over them who will tend them…" That's the promise for these sheep, and soldiers aren't mentioned.
The LORD says, "…I will raise up for David a righteous Branch, and He will reign wisely as King…" So the word for the blank is King. Reigning is exactly what the verse says the Branch will do.
Prophet is a fair guess, but it's not the word here. The LORD says the righteous Branch "…will reign wisely as King…" Reigning is a king's work.

Priest is a fair guess, but it's not the word the LORD uses here. He says the righteous Branch "…will reign wisely as King and will administer justice and righteousness in the land." So the word is King.
That's the other half. The LORD says "…Israel will dwell securely." Think of the flock earlier, scattered and afraid. This is what the LORD promises for the Branch's days.
Apart is closer to the old trouble than to the promise. The sheep were scattered, and in the Branch's days the LORD says Israel "…will dwell securely." So the word for the second blank is securely.
